notes.subject: car
notes.text: The car shows side mirrors, a roof rack and black tape on the end of the rear right bar; the Ghana car has tape on the front right bar instead.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Signs, bollards and poles follow the style of the mother country in Europe, since this is an overseas department.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A steep, volcanic tropical island: roads hug the coast with lush green mountains close by, and palms, ferns, pines at height and flowering plants.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Six bus stop designs exist (yellow, L-shaped, pink, orange, green, red); yellow is the most common and helps a region guess when seen alone.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sugarcane plantations occur in two areas, the northeast and the southwest; the southwest is more built up.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A town inside a caldera, ringed by a wall of mountains under overcast skies.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A rectangular blur on the front camera appears in all coverage north of Saint-Louis.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The northwestern N1 is a divided road with a distinct ridge to the southeast and the ocean to the northwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The volcano road has a Mars-like landscape of brown-red soil, scattered shrubs and white stones along the road.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A winding dark dirt forest track with grass down its middle and dense pines and eucalyptus.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The east is the least populated: a single-carriageway N2 with dense vegetation or wide treeless landscape.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Intersection bollards differ between the two biggest towns: black in the western one, green with white balls on top in the capital.
